target_customer: Indian couples and households (married, engaged, live-in, roommates) who share expenses; revenue from card interchange and partner offers
problem: Couples juggle separate accounts, cards and expense tools, while bank joint accounts involve paperwork and minimum balances.
business_model: Consumer prepaid joint account and co-branded RuPay cards issued through a licensed PPI partner, earning interchange and partnership fees (exact model not stated by sources)
product_category: Consumer fintech: digital joint account and shared expense app for couples

founders.name: Kushagra Manglik
prior_employers: IBM Research (Research Software Engineer, AI for Supply Chain team, nearly two years)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page, which lists him as Founder/CEO and says he has papers and 6 patents. Another aggregator labels Sarkar as CEO, so titles conflict.

founders.name: Srinivas Sarkar
founders.background_notes: Source: YC launch post and Entrepreneur India profile (which says the two met in the Entrepreneur First cohort). Named Srini on the YC page.

competitors.name: Splitwise
competitors.what: Expense-splitting app couples use for shared costs
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; named by the founders as an alternative and by users who switched

competitors.name: Traditional bank joint accounts
competitors.what: Bank joint accounts, described by the founders as cumbersome to open and expensive to maintain

competitors.name: Fibbl
competitors.what: Bangalore neobank for couples with shared budgeting, money pooling and joint goals

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed payments integrations with a PPI issuer, RuPay cards and BBPS bill pay in a regulated environment, but built on partner rails rather than owning a license.

defensibility.rationale: The product depends on partner rails (LivQuik, NPCI, RuPay), which any rival can also use, and Fibbl had a similar couples proposition.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or incumbent copy found; the company reported 8,000 joint accounts after a September 2023 launch.

market_need_then: Founders cite over 10 million Indian weddings a year and pain from joint account paperwork and minimum balances; the public launch followed in September 2023.

branding.domain_note: Uses coupl.money rather than coupl.com; no history found.

identity.visual_style: Co-branded matching card pair for two partners
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and inclusive, open to married, dating, long-distance and same-sex couples; mission of the most financially-savvy generation of couples

branding.brand_signature: Two matching co-branded debit cards for a couple
branding.community_and_virality: Founders say they reached 8,000 joint accounts with no ad spend (company claim); a user switching from Splitwise story is shown on the site.

brand_strength.rationale: A short evocative coined name with a clear couples promise and coverage in FinTech Futures, PYMNTS and Entrepreneur India, but no evidence yet of large community pull.

pivots.why: Per a 2023 Entrepreneur India profile as summarized in search results; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Coupl joined YC in S22, launched its joint account publicly in September 2023 on a partner PPI issuer and reported 8,000 accounts by its YC launch post. No verified priced round was found beyond aggregator figures, and the company remains an eight person active team. The outcome is open; the main risks are dependence on partner rails and a small paying base.
notes: Funding is aggregator-only and conflicting: Seedtable says 554K USD seed on 2022-04-12 (YC and Entrepreneur First), Bouncewatch says 55K pre-seed on 2022-03-31 and 500K pre-seed on 2022-08-01. Unverified, so no rounds recorded. Competitor sources: the YC launch post is dated later than the batch (it says about three years ago; a search summary dated it May 2024), and the Fibbl article has no date found. They are kept because the rivals existed around founding but dates are unverified. Pivot is from a search summary of Entrepreneur India, not read in full. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news found.
